title: Low and high ice maxima showed no clear pair concurrence difference across four Great Lakes in 1973-2025
abstract: We tested whether low annual ice maxima occurred together across Superior, Michigan, Huron and Erie more often than high maxima. We used 53 winters in a fixed NOAA GLERL table. Lower and upper quarter weights were set within 1973-1998 and 1999-2025, with equal weights at ties. Mean weighted pair concurrence was 0.839 for low ice and 0.767 for high ice. The difference was 0.072. A 95% interval from 20,000 five-year block resamples was -0.106 to 0.257. Thus, this test gave no clear difference. All planned sensitivity intervals included zero. Without Erie, the point difference was 0.002. The result does not show equal tail dependence or identify a physical cause. Short records, changing chart methods, ties and within-period climate trends limit inference. The package includes code, source hashes, aggregate results, primary resample scores, a figure and separate arithmetic checks. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Weighted pair concurrence for low and high annual ice maxima, and low-minus-high differences under all planned checks. Bars and points use 95% block intervals. Every difference interval includes zero. The dashed left line is an independence reference, not a fitted climate model.

citations.reason: We use its source inventory and the same fixed shared table. It tests peak date spread; this study tests concurrence of low and high amounts. Data overlap, so this is not independent replication.
